rationale: The original itinerary has been modified to accommodate the confirmed disruption where the National Gallery of Art is unavailable. The activity 'national_gallery' has been removed from the sequence. To maintain chronological flow and minimize travel time, the subsequent activities (National Museum of American History, National Museum of Natural History, World War II Memorial, and Lincoln Memorial) have been shifted forward by the duration of the removed activity (90 minutes). This preserves the relative order of the remaining original activities while ensuring they can be visited within the scheduled day.
preserved_constraints: Preservation of all unaffected original activities: american_history, natural_history, wwii_memorial, lincoln_memorial.
Preservation of mandatory constraint for natural_history (mandatory: true).
Preservation of travel modes and estimated durations between remaining activities as originally calculated.
violated_constraints: The original activity 'national_gallery' was removed due to confirmed unavailability, violating the implicit constraint of preserving all scheduled activities unless they are unavailable.

trade_offs: Benefit: The itinerary now reflects the reality that the National Gallery is closed, preventing wasted time at an unavailable venue. The remaining activities remain feasible within the day.

Trade-off: The original schedule for subsequent activities has been compressed by 90 minutes. For example, the visit to the National Museum of Natural History now starts at 10:50 AM instead of 13:20 PM. This may reduce the time available for other unlisted activities or rest periods if the user intended to extend the day.
Trade-off: The proposal does not include a replacement activity for the National Gallery. Adding an alternative would require verified availability data which is currently absent.
assumptions: Assumption: The remaining original activities (american_history, natural_history, wwii_memorial, lincoln_memorial) are open and operational on 2026-11-07. This assumption is not independently verified by the retrieved evidence.
